content: Rifampin interacts with various drugs by influencing their metabolism or transport mechanisms, often leading to reduced drug levels or effects. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions: 1. Escitalopram: Rifampin reduces escitalopram levels by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Esomeprazole: Rifampin decreases esomeprazole levels by influencing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Estradiol: Rifampin lowers estradiol levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 4. Estradiol Vaginal: Rifampin reduces estradiol vaginal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Conjugated Synthetic Estrogens: Rifampin decreases their levels through the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 6. Esterified Estrogens: Rifampin reduces their levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Estropipate: Rifampin lowers estropipate levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. 8. Eszopiclone: Rifampin decreases eszopiclone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Zopiclone AUC is reduced by 80% with rifampin, and a similar effect is expected for eszopiclone. 9. Ethosuximide: Rifampin reduces ethosuximide levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 10. Ethotoin: Rifampin decreases ethotoin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Etoposide: Rifampin reduces etoposide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 12. Etravirine: Rifampin decreases etravirine levels by influencing CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Eucalyptus: Rifampin reduces eucalyptus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 14. Exemestane: Rifampin decreases exemestane levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients on potent CYP3A4 inducers, the recommended exemestane dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. 15. Fenfluramine: Rifampin reduces fenfluramine levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with serotonin-increasing drugs may elevate the risk of serotonin syndrome. 16. Fentanyl: Rifampin decreases fentanyl levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to reduced fentanyl efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. After stopping the inducer, fentanyl levels may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. 17. Fentanyl (Intranasal, Transdermal, Transmucosal): Rifampin reduces fentanyl levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Finasteride: Rifampin decreases finasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 19. Flibanserin: Rifampin reduces flibanserin levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 20. Fluconazole: Rifampin decreases fluconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 21. Fludrocortisone: Rifampin reduces fludrocortisone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 22. Flurazepam: Rifampin decreases flurazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 23. Fluvastatin: Rifampin increases fluvastatin toxicity. OATP1B1 inhibitors may elevate the risk of myopathy. Monitoring is advised. 24. Fosphenytoin: Rifampin reduces fosphenytoin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 25. Fostamatinib: Rifampin increases fostamatinib levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring for toxicities is required, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. 26. Gefitinib: Rifampin decreases gefitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily with strong CYP3A4 inducers and resume 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the inducer. 27. Gentamicin: Rifampin reduces gentamicin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 28. Glimepiride, Glipizide, Glyburide: Rifampin decreases their levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is required. 29. Guanfacine: Rifampin reduces guanfacine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. For ADHD patients, consider doubling the guanfacine dose when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 30. Haloperidol: Rifampin decreases haloperidol levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 31. Hydrocodone: Rifampin reduces hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers may increase hydrocodone levels, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 32. Hydrocortisone: Rifampin decreases hydrocortisone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 33. Ifosfamide: Rifampin increases ifosfamide toxicity by affecting CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inducers may elevate neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolite formation. Close monitoring and dose adjustments are recommended. 34. Imatinib: Rifampin reduces imatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 35. Imipramine: Rifampin decreases imipramine levels by influencing CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 36. Indinavir: Rifampin reduces indinavir levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 37. Iptacopan: Rifampin decreases iptacopan levels by increasing metabolism. CYP2C8 inducers may reduce iptacopan efficacy. Monitoring is required. 38. Irinotecan: Rifampin reduces irinotecan levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 39. Isradipine: Rifampin decreases isradipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 40. Istradefylline: Rifampin increases istradefylline levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 41. Itraconazole: Rifampin reduces itraconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 42. Ivacaftor: Rifampin increases ivacaftor levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 43. Ivermectin: Rifampin reduces ivermectin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 44. Ketamine: Rifampin decreases ketamine levels by affecting CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 45. Ketoconazole: Rifampin reduces ketoconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 46. Lamotrigine: Rifampin decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing metabolism and hepatic clearance. Monitoring is necessary. 47. Lapatinib: Rifampin reduces lapatinib levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 48. Lemborexant: Rifampin decreases lemborexant levels by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 49. Lesinurad: Rifampin reduces lesinurad levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 50. Levamlodipine: Rifampin decreases levamlodipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 51. Levonorgestrel (Intrauterine, Oral): Rifampin reduces levonorgestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; alternative or backup contraception is recommended. 52. Lidocaine: Rifampin decreases lidocaine levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 53. Linagliptin: Rifampin reduces linagliptin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended. 54. Lofepramine: Rifampin decreases lofepramine levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is required. 55. Lomitapide: Rifampin increases lomitapide levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 56. Loperamide: Rifampin reduces loperamide levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 57. Losartan: Rifampin decreases losartan levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 58. Lovastatin: Rifampin reduces lovastatin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 59. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Rifampin affects lumacaftor/ivacaftor metabolism via CYP2B6. Monitoring is necessary. 60. Maraviroc: Rifampin reduces maraviroc levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 61. Marijuana: Rifampin decreases marijuana levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 62. Mavorixafor: Rifampin increases mavorixafor levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 63. Medroxyprogesterone: Rifampin reduces medroxyprogesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 64. Mefloquine: Rifampin decreases mefloquine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 65. Melatonin: Rifampin reduces melatonin levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 66. Mestranol: Rifampin decreases mestranol levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 67. Methadone: Rifampin decreases methadone levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 68. Methylprednisolone: Rifampin reduces methylprednisolone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 69. Metoprolol: Rifampin decreases metoprolol levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 70. Mexiletine: Rifampin reduces mexiletine levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 71. Miconazole (Vaginal): Rifampin decreases miconazole levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 72. Mifepristone: Rifampin reduces mifepristone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 73. Mipomersen: Rifampin increases mipomersen toxicity. Both drugs may elevate hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 74. Mirtazapine: Rifampin decreases mirtazapine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 75. Momelotinib: Rifampin increases momelotinib toxicity. OATP1B1/B3 inhibitors may elevate momelotinib plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 76. Montelukast: Rifampin reduces montelukast levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 77. Nafcillin: Rifampin's effects may be reduced by nafcillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitoring is required. 78. Nefazodone: Rifampin decreases nefazodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 79. Neomycin (PO): Rifampin reduces neomycin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 80. Nifedipine: Rifampin decreases nifedipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 81. Nilotinib: Rifampin reduces nilotinib levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 82. Nimodipine: Rifampin decreases nimodipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 83. Nitrendipine: Rifampin reduces nitrendipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 84. Olanzapine: Rifampin decreases olanzapine levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 85. Oliceridine: Rifampin reduces oliceridine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 86. Omeprazole: Rifampin decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 87. Ondansetron: Rifampin reduces ondansetron levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 88. Osilodrostat: Rifampin decreases osilodrostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 89. Ospemifene: Rifampin reduces ospemifene levels by affecting CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 90. Oxybutynin: Rifampin decreases oxybutynin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 91. Oxycodone: Rifampin reduces oxycodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 92. Paclitaxel: Rifampin decreases paclitaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, and other mechanisms. Monitoring is necessary. 93. Paliperidone: Rifampin reduces paliperidone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 94. Pantoprazole: Rifampin decreases pantoprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 95. Parecoxib: Rifampin reduces parecoxib levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 96. Paromomycin: Rifampin reduces paromomycin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 97. Pentobarbital: Rifampin decreases pentobarbital levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is required. 98. Phenobarbital: Rifampin reduces phenobarbital levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 99. Phenytoin: Rifampin decreases phenytoin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 100. Pimavanserin: Rifampin reduces pimavanserin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible. Monitor for reduced efficacy and consider dosage increases. 101. Pimozide: Rifampin decreases pimozide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 102. Pioglitazone: Rifampin reduces pioglitazone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 103. Pitavastatin: Rifampin increases pitavastatin levels by decreasing metabolism. Do not exceed 2 mg/day. Monitoring is required. 104. Pitolisant: Rifampin reduces pitolisant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 105. Polatuzumab Vedotin: Rifampin decreases polatuzumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 106. Ponatinib: Rifampin increases ponatinib levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 107. Posaconazole: Rifampin reduces posaconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 108. Pravastatin: Rifampin increases pravastatin toxicity. OATP1B1 inhibitors may elevate the risk of myopathy. Monitoring is advised. 109. Prednisolone: Rifampin reduces prednisolone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is required. 110. Prednisone: Rifampin decreases prednisone levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is necessary. 111. Pretomanid: Rifampin increases pretomanid levels. Monitor for drug-related adverse effects. 112. Primidone: Rifampin reduces primidone levels by increasing metabolism. Monitoring is required. 113. Pyrazinamide: Rifampin interacts with pyrazinamide. Monitoring is necessary.
